summary: A 1962 steel cab now tops Black Mountain; the first lookout there dates to 1926 and was moved to Barton Peak. Volunteers staff it in fire season.

facts.design: CL-100 steel cab with flat corrugated metal roof and metal mesh catwalk on a solid rock outcrop (completed 1962); the earlier structure was a California Region 5 Plan 4AR cabin on a 10 ft open timber tower
facts.status_note: Forest Service current-conditions notice, read 2026-10-08, says 'Closed for the season'; the lookout is otherwise standing and volunteer-staffed in fire season.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, San Bernardino National Forest, San Jacinto Ranger District

staffing.status: Volunteer-staffed (Lookout Host Program) in fire season; Forest Service says usually open 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.; NHLR says Lookout Hosts seven days a week

access.note: Walk-in public access during the staffed season, generally Memorial Day to November; Forest Service current conditions read 'Closed for the season'

visit.trail_note: About half a mile on foot from Boulder Basin Campground (1-mile round trip on a dirt road), or the longer Black Mountain Trail

events.note: First lookout on Black Mountain per the Forest Service; the third lookout built on the San Bernardino National Forest. NHLR dates the original cabin to the late 1910s or early 1920s
Rita Morris of Hemet announced for the summer season, described as the first woman lookout in Southern California (May 1, 1928 newspaper item, quoted on a lookout history site)
A May 31, 1929 newspaper item says Morris had again gone on duty at the Black Mountain station (secondhand, via lookout history site)
Original Plan 4AR cabin on a 10 ft open timber tower moved to Barton Peak; NHLR says 1934, the Forest Service says 1935
Current CL-100 steel cab completed on Black Mountain (NHLR and Forest Service); a bronze plaque reportedly dated 1962 is noted in a photo log, not used here
The Barton Peak location was discontinued when the new lookout was completed on Black Mountain
Registered October 1, 1998 as NHLR US 289, CA 22

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Service dates the first lookout on the site to 1926; NHLR says the original cabin was built in the late 1910s or early 1920s. Both give 1962 for the current cab, which the record keeps as the 'built' date.
NHLR says the structure was moved in 1934; the Forest Service says the original lookout was disassembled and rebuilt on Barton Peak in 1935. The story gives both years.

NHLR says Lookout Hosts staff the lookout seven days a week. The Forest Service says volunteers staff it and it is usually open 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. during fire season. The sources do not reconcile; visitors should check.

The record's 2327.1 m matches NHLR (7,635 ft). The Forest Service page gives 7,772 ft (about 2,369 m), and a photo log repeats 7772 ft. The record was not changed; an editor should decide which figure to use.

notes_for_editor: The sbnfa.com page in the brief returned HTTP 403 and was not read. The current-conditions 'Closed for the season' line on the Forest Service page was read on 2026-10-08 and may not reflect a later reopening. NHLR's undated 'seven days a week' staffing claim conflicts with the Forest Service's fire-season hours. The NHLR description says the cab was restored after the 1980s but gives no year, so no restoration event is recorded. A photo log (peakbagging.com, May 2022) gives a 14 ft cab on a 20 ft steel tower; that was not used because it is a single hobbyist source that conflicts with the NHLR cab dimensions, which were not quoted in the story. The 1928 and 1929 Rita Morris items are secondhand quotations on a lookout history site; the originals were not checked. No notable fires were found in the sources.
